title: Boss: The Wrong Match
story: The packing list shows customers beside products they never bought. One join condition links the wrong columns.
goal: Fix the query so it lists customer and product (use these column names) for every order.
starter:
SELECT c.name, p.name
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.id = c.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: Run it and compare: customers should match o.customer_id, not o.id.
Give the two result columns the names customer and product.
SELECT c.name AS customer, p.name AS product FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id;
socratic: Which column in orders points at a customer?
What names must the output columns have?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what was wrong with the query, and how did you fix it?
solution: SELECT c.name AS customer, p.name AS product FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id;
alt: SELECT c.name AS customer, p.name AS product FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id;
